title: Standard internal contradictions and section-coverage claims
cluster_summary: Sections of the standard, its playbooks and its summaries were edited one at a time, and duplicated lists (frozen stores, Tier 2 members, applicability enumerations, ordinals, the pre-adoption launcher census) have drifted apart. Every fix lands in WowAddonStandards: one documentation-and-playbook pass covering AUDIT.md, launcher.md, slash-commands.md, documentation.md §3/§6/§8, library-stack.md §7, NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md and the two summaries. Must or should: the stale launcher 'expect findings' wording (WAS-A-08), the §6 frozen-store list and sweep (WAS-A-14) and the scaffold runner comment (WAS-R-05). The rest are cheap consistency fixes to fold into the same pass. LibKa0s and dev-copilot need no change.

verdicts.assessment: All 11 addons have adopted the launcher and disabled latch on LibKa0s v1.70.0. Even so, AUDIT.md:542/:652-653 and launcher.md:92 still tell auditors to expect failures everywhere, which primes the next audits to file false findings.
verdicts.remediation: Delete the forward-looking wording in AUDIT.md:542 ('expected to be non-compliant until it adopts'), AUDIT.md:652-653 ('Expect findings here in every audit until the adoption pass lands') and launcher.md:92 ('non-compliant ... until it adopts'). Replace it with the post-adoption expectation that the audit verifies the latch. Keep the slash-commands.md:200 census and the launcher §5 'blocked rather than overdue' paragraph, but rewrite both in the past tense as history (the 2026-09-16 pre-adoption sweep). Check: grepping for those phrases returns nothing.

verdicts.assessment: The ordinals at documentation.md:170 and :347 contradict the list at :148, but nobody misreads a section because of them. It is a cosmetic fix to fold into the documentation.md pass.
verdicts.remediation: Drop the ordinals at documentation.md:170 and :347 and refer to the sections by name, so they cannot drift again.

verdicts.assessment: documentation-§6 keeps its own four-store exemption list, while documentation-§3 names seven stores. Run as written, the §6 sweep would touch frozen docs/superpowers/ bundles (140 dotted-§ hits across 4 addons). It also wrongly exempts the live docs/automated-tests/README.md and RESULTS.md. harvests/ falls under the MUST half only; the sweep finds 0 hits there.
verdicts.remediation: Have §6 cite documentation-§3's frozen-store list by reference instead of keeping a copy. Add a clause for a repo's own frozen stores (harvests/, standards/_raw/). Narrow the automated-tests exemption to docs/automated-tests/<run>/. Replace the sweep with a git ls-files pipeline that excludes every frozen store.

verdicts.assessment: The exhaustiveness claim holds at file granularity, since every file in the STANDARDS.md Sections list is placed. Only localization-§1-§4 are ambiguous at subsection level, and documentation-§9 already classifies itself. The real defect is the arithmetic at :698 ('six of ten', 'five', 'the other five'), which counts Module Map twice. The DC-A-15 trigger contradiction sits in the same table.
verdicts.remediation: Fix the :698 arithmetic so Module Map is counted once (five sections dropped, five kept, one of them reinterpreted). State explicitly that any subsection not listed applies unchanged, and either place localization-§1-§4 under 'Does not apply' or reword the claim as file-granular. Do this in the same edit as DC-A-15 and LK-A-10.

verdicts.assessment: documentation.md's Tier 2 table does list perf-analysis/README.md, and both summaries leave it out of their Tier 2 parentheticals. But both summaries name it, with its trigger, among the verification-and-record docs, so the doc is not missing and the CLAUDE.md:141 rule is not broken. Only the cross-membership goes unstated.
verdicts.remediation: In CLAUDE.md and EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md, add a note to each Tier 2 parenthetical that perf-analysis/README.md is also a Tier 2 member (its trigger is already stated under verification-and-record). Fold this into the doc pass.

verdicts.assessment: The scaffold runner comment at NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md:1072 says a missing suite is skipped. testing-§9 and LibKa0s testkit/framework.lua loadSuites both raise on a missing suite, and the comment gets copied into every newly scaffolded addon. It is a one-line fix.
verdicts.remediation: Rewrite the comment: a suite named in the runner but missing from disk raises, and a suite deliberately left out must be declared pending (testing-§9).

verdicts.assessment: The exhaustiveness claim holds at file granularity, and unplaced subsections default to 'applies', so nothing changes in LibKa0s. Checking it turned up a real mislabel: the library-stack.md:223 row labeled documentation-§5 describes §6's content, and the §4 row at :261 then claims §6 is 'already named'.
verdicts.remediation: In WowAddonStandards library-stack-§7, relabel the :223 row 'documentation-§5, documentation-§6' so the §4 row's cross-reference holds. Optionally state that unlisted subsections apply unchanged. Do not track this as a LibKa0s item.

verdicts.assessment: documentation.md:703 names three re-read triggers and then says the trigger is only 'the first .lua file'. That leaves open whether dev-copilot's Python helpers and their tests oblige lint/testing/automated-tests. It is ungraded and nothing is broken; reconcile it in the same documentation-§8 edit.
verdicts.remediation: Make the documentation-§8 row state a single trigger, either 'any of: a Lua file, a test harness, or a script complex enough to have a failure mode' or 'the first .lua file', and remove the other sentence. dev-copilot changes only if the reconciled trigger brings it into scope.
